passage: At the Lisbon nursery door, two-year-old Alejandro wraps both arms around his mother Olga's leg and screams when she steps back. He cries long after the door closes. At pickup he runs to her, then shoves her hand away and wails, then climbs into her arms and grips her collar tight. Olga holds him through the kicking and the clinging, humming softly, until his breaths slow.

qa.q: Where does Alejandro cling to Olga's leg?
qa.a: He clings to her leg at the Lisbon nursery door.

qa.q: What might Alejandro be feeling at pickup when he shoves Olga's hand away and then grips her collar?
qa.a: He seems both angry and desperate for comfort, as if he is not sure she will stay.

qa.q: What did Olga choose to do when he pushed her away, and why does it help?
qa.a: She stayed and held him through the kicking and clinging, humming, which shows him her comfort is steady.

qa.q: What is it like for Olga when Alejandro pushes her away and clings at the same time?
qa.a: It can be tiring and confusing, but she keeps calm and patient until he settles.

grounding: A toddler screams when his mother leaves and, on her return, swings between anger and clinging before settling in her arms.

passage: I'm Ayesha, from the flat opposite. Every morning when her Papa leaves for work, little Arohi, two, screams at the grille and bangs it with both hands. Her Dadi can't calm her for ages. When he comes back in the evening, she clings to his leg, then slaps his arm and turns away, then cries to be picked up again. Maybe she isn't sure he will come back each time. I don't really know.

qa.q: What does Arohi do at the grille when her Papa leaves?
qa.a: She screams at the grille and bangs it with both hands.

qa.q: What might Arohi be worried about when she slaps her Papa and then cries to be held?
qa.a: She may be unsure he will keep coming back, so she feels angry and needy at the same time.

qa.q: What could Arohi's Papa try to make goodbyes easier?
qa.a: He could keep a short, calm goodbye each morning and greet her the same warm way each evening, so his return starts to feel steady.

qa.q: How might Arohi's Dadi feel during the long mornings after Papa leaves?
qa.a: She is likely tired and worried, since she can't calm Arohi for ages.

grounding: A neighbour describes a toddler who screams when her father leaves and alternates between clinging and anger when he returns, and only guesses at why.

passage: At the daycare door in Tucson, Camila wrapped both arms around her dad's leg and screamed as Jamal tried to leave. The teacher lifted her; she arched her back and wailed until her face was red. When Jamal came back at five, Camila ran to him, then hit his chest and turned away. A minute later she was clutching his shirt again, refusing to be put down, eyes on the door all the way to the car.

qa.q: What did Camila do when Jamal tried to leave?
qa.a: She wrapped both arms around her dad's leg and screamed.

qa.q: What might Camila be feeling when Jamal comes back?
qa.a: She seems both relieved and angry: she runs to him, hits him, then clings, as if unsure he will stay.

qa.q: How could Jamal help Camila feel safer at goodbyes?
qa.a: Keep goodbyes short and the same each day, come back when promised and stay calm through her anger.

qa.q: What is it like for Jamal when Camila hits him and turns away?
qa.a: He may feel hurt or confused, even though her anger shows how upsetting the parting was for her.

grounding: Shows a toddler who cries hard at parting and swings between clinging and anger on the caregiver's return.

passage:
Monday: when Mehak left for work, Jaya howled at the window and would not let Nani hold her. In the evening she clung to Mummy's dupatta and screamed whenever Mehak stood up.
Wednesday: Mehak waved and said, "After your nap, Mummy comes," then left. Jaya cried, stamped and pushed Nani's hand away.
Saturday: Jaya cried at the goodbye, then sat on Nani's lap with the peg puzzle. When Mehak came home, Jaya hit her arm once, then climbed into her lap.

qa.q: What did Jaya play with on Nani's lap on Saturday?
qa.a: The peg puzzle.

qa.q: Why might Jaya scream whenever Mehak stood up on Monday evening?
qa.a: She seems scared that Mummy will leave again, so she stays on alert and clings.

qa.q: What small step seems to help Jaya over the week?
qa.a: Mehak's same short goodbye, telling her when Mummy comes back, which makes partings more predictable.

qa.q: How might Nani feel when Jaya pushes her hand away?
qa.a: Nani may feel a little helpless or rejected, while knowing Jaya is upset about Mummy, not about her.

grounding: Shows across several days a toddler who cries hard at parting and mixes clinging with anger on return.

passage: Shalini only went down to the vegetable cart, but Ishita flung herself at the flat door, shrieking "Amma!" until the neighbour peeped out. Paati couldn't settle her with biscuits or songs. When Shalini came back up with the bag of tomatoes, Ishita shoved her away and kicked, then grabbed her hair and would not let go. All evening Ishita followed her even to the bathroom door, whimpering whenever it closed.

qa.q: Where did Shalini go?
qa.a: Down to the vegetable cart.

qa.q: Why might Ishita whimper whenever the bathroom door closed?
qa.a: She seems afraid Amma will disappear again, so she stays anxious and watchful all evening.

qa.q: How could Shalini make short trips easier for Ishita?
qa.a: Say a calm, same-every-time goodbye with when she will return, and keep her promise so Ishita learns she comes back.

qa.q: What is it like for Paati when biscuits and songs do not work?
qa.a: Paati may feel worried and helpless, since nothing she tries can replace Amma for Ishita in that moment.

grounding: Illustrates a toddler who cries intensely at a short parting and alternates clinging and anger after the caregiver returns.

passage:
"Ammi going to work now, Kashish. Back after your nap."
"No! Ammi! No!" Kashish clutched Farida's kurta, screaming.
Nani lifted her. "Come, jaan, see the birds."
Kashish kicked and cried until she fell asleep.
Evening. "Kashish, I'm back!"
Kashish ran, grabbed Farida's legs, then hit her arm. "Bad Ammi!"
"You were angry I went," Farida said softly.
Kashish sobbed, climbed into her lap, and would not let go.

qa.q: Who lifted Kashish after Farida left?
qa.a: Nani lifted her.

qa.q: How did Kashish feel when Farida came back?
qa.a: She was angry and upset, hitting Farida's arm and saying "Bad Ammi!", yet she also clung to her lap.

qa.q: What did Farida do well when Kashish hit her?
qa.a: She stayed calm and named the feeling, "You were angry I went," instead of scolding, which let Kashish come close again.

qa.q: What might the day be like for Nani?
qa.a: Nani has a hard day with a toddler who kicks and cries until she sleeps, and needs a lot of patience.

grounding: Shows a toddler who cries hard when her mother leaves and on return swings between hitting and clinging, unsure comfort will stay.
